final_message:
I fixed one bug in `wrap` in `src/wrap.py`, but I haven't run it or any tests.

When a word was longer than `width` and it was the first word on a line, `wrap` added an empty string to the output. This happened because the "does this overflow?" check also ran when the current line was empty. For example, `wrap("abcdefgh hi", 5)` returned `["", "abcdefgh hi"...]`-style output with a blank line in it. The check now only applies when the line already has content (`if cur and ...`), so an over-long word goes on its own line.

I left over-long words unbroken, so they still extend past `width`. If you'd rather split them at `width`, say so and I'll add that.
